record.what_it_does: Binance's API lets developers programmatically place trades, manage accounts/wallets, and stream market data across its Spot, Margin, Futures, and Options crypto exchange products.
record.auth_notes: Signed requests use an API key (X-MBX-APIKEY header) plus a request signature computed with HMAC SHA256, RSA, or Ed25519 depending on the key type generated in API Management; there is also a separate 'Binance ID' OAuth2 login flow used only for third-party social sign-in/profile retrieval (user:email, user:address scopes), not for trading/account API calls, so it is not the primary method for an agent toolkit.
record.access_notes: Any Binance account holder can generate API keys for free in API Management; a free Spot Testnet and a no-cost Demo mode are also available for building/testing without a funded account. Full production trading requires normal account KYC verification (standard for any user, not a special developer-approval gate).
record.webhooks_notes: Not used for core Spot/Futures trading (which relies on WebSocket user-data streams), but documented webhook callbacks exist for specific products like Binance Connect (order status change events) and KYC-SaaS.

evidence.quote: Secure endpoints require a valid API key to be specified and authenticated.
